children: , the database and AI-cloud provider, faced a tougher funding backdrop as spreads on AI-linked debt climbed to roughly 115 basis points. Shares edged about 0.1% higher to $148.73 Tuesday morning. The chart places Oracle 22.5% below its GF Value estimate of $191.91, signaling potential upside if its cloud expansion translates into stronger cash flow.

The market is charging AI borrowers a premium. The sector's average spread sits 37 basis pointsor about 47%above the broader investment-grade market's 78 basis points. Oracle nevertheless has real growth behind its spending: its latest quarter generated $11.6 billion in cloud revenue, up 62%, even as aggressive infrastructure investment keeps the company returning to debt markets.

This is not a default alarm. It is a price-of-capital warning. Reuters said investors want extra compensation for heavy issuance and uncertain AI returns, while the industrywide spread does not reveal Oracle's specific borrowing cost. Clearer funding guidance, customer prepayments and faster conversion of cloud demand into cash could give Oracle a genuine edge as lenders become pickier.

title: Oracle Edged Higher While AI Borrowers Pay 37 Extra Basis Points
